arxiv-1511-01933.title: Interface control of electronic transport across the magnetic phase transition in SrRuO 3 /SrTiO 3 heterointerface
arxiv-1511-01933.creator: S. Roy 1 , C. Autieri 2 , B. Sanyal 2 , T. Banerjee 1
arxiv-1511-01933.description: Abstract The emerging material class of complex-oxides, where manipulation of physical properties lead to new functionalities at their heterointerfaces, is expected to open new frontiers in Spintronics. For example, SrRuO 3 is a promising material where external stimuli like strain, temperature and structural distortions control the stability of electronic and magnetic states, across its magnetic phase transition, useful for Spintronics.

arxiv-1903-03066.title: Group Theoretical Settling of Spin Zero Relativistic Particle Theories
arxiv-1903-03066.creator: Giuseppe Nisticò
arxiv-1903-03066.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Giuseppe Nisticò. In order to avoid the difficulties encountered by relativistic quantum theory of single particles, we pursue a deductive development of the theory from physical principles, without canonical quantization, by making use of group-theoretical methods. Our work has pointed out the necessity of new classes of irreducible representations of the Poincaré group the quantum theory of a particle can be based on. For spin 0 particle, four inequivalent theories are completely determined, with fundamental differences with respect to Klein-Gordon theory.

arxiv-2211-08976.title: Generating Stable and Collision-Free Policies through Lyapunov Function Learning
arxiv-2211-08976.creator: Alexandre Coulombe, Hsiu-Chin Lin
arxiv-2211-08976.description: Abstract The need for rapid and reliable robot deployment is on the rise. Imitation Learning (IL) has become popular for producing motion planning policies from a set of demonstrations. However, many methods in IL are not guaranteed to produce stable policies.

arxiv-2212-14703.title: Quantum simulation of partial differential equations via Schrödingerisation: technical details
arxiv-2212-14703.creator: Shi Jin, Nana Liu, Yue Yu
arxiv-2212-14703.description: Abstract We study a new method– called Schrödingerisation introduced in [ 25 ] – for solving general linear partial differential equations with quantum simulation. This method converts linear partial differential equations into a ‘Schrödingerised’ or Hamiltonian system, using a new and simple transformation called the warped phase transformation .

arxiv-2307-05184.title: Sporadic simple groups as flag-transitive automorphism groups of symmetric designs Thanks: Corresponding author: S.H. Alavi
arxiv-2307-05184.creator: Seyed Hassan Alavi, Ashraf Daneshkhah
arxiv-2307-05184.description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Seyed Hassan Alavi, Ashraf Daneshkhah. In this article, we study symmetric designs admitting flag-transitive, point-imprimitive almost simple automorphism groups with socle sporadic simple groups. As a corollary, we present a classification of symmetric designs admitting flag-transitive automorphism group whose socle is a sporadic simple group, and in conclusion, there are exactly seven such designs, one of which admits a point-imprimitive automorphism group and the remaining are point-primitive. arxiv-2401-13146.title: Locality enhanced dynamic biasing and sampling strategies for contextual ASR
arxiv-2401-13146.creator: Md Asif Jalal, Pablo Peso Parada, George Pavlidis, Vasileios Moschopoulos, Karthikeyan Saravanan, Chrysovalantis-Giorgos Kontoulis, Jisi Zhang, Anastasios Drosou, Gil Ho Lee, Jungin Lee, Seokyeong Jung
arxiv-2401-13146.description: Abstract Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) still face challenges when recognizing time-variant rare-phrases. Contextual biasing (CB) modules bias ASR model towards such contextually-relevant phrases. During training, a list of biasing phrases are selected from a large pool of phrases following a sampling strategy.

arxiv-2510-07706.title: Large Language Models Meet Virtual Cell: A Survey
arxiv-2510-07706.creator: Krinos Li, Xianglu Xiao, Shenglong Deng, Lucas He, Zijun Zhong, Yuanjie Zou, Zhonghao Zhan, Zheng Hui, Weiye Bao, Guang Yang
arxiv-2510-07706.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Krinos Li, Xianglu Xiao, Shenglong Deng, Lucas He, Zijun Zhong, Yuanjie Zou, Zhonghao Zhan, Zheng Hui, Weiye Bao, Guang Yang. Large language models (LLMs) are transforming cellular biology by enabling the development of "virtual cells"—computational systems that represent, predict, and reason about cellular states and behaviors. This work provides a comprehensive review of LLMs for virtual cell modeling.

pmc-11394995.title: Non-Covalent Interaction of Folic Acid and 5-Methyltetrahydrofolate with Caseinates Improves the Folates Stability Studied by Multi-Spectroscopic Analysis and Molecular Docking
pmc-11394995.creator: Linlin He, Yuqian Yan, Gang Zhang, Yanna Zhao, Fa Zhao, Zhuang Ding, Zhengping Wang
pmc-11394995.description: Folates, a crucial B-group vitamin, serve as a significant functional food supplement. Nevertheless, considerable obstacles persist in improving folates stability in liquid products. In this study, folic acid (FA) and 5-methyltetrahydrofolate (MTFA), two approved sources of folates, were encapsulated with sodium caseinate (NaCas) to enhance their stability.

pmc-12621335.title: Attachment representations in Afghan refugees undergoing psychological treatment: a pilot study
pmc-12621335.creator: Thomas Egger, Manuela Gander, Britta Dumser, Theresa Koch, Anna Buchheim
pmc-12621335.description: Background: Refugees are at elevated risk of trauma-related disorders. Unresolved attachment is a vulnerability factor for post-traumatic stress, yet its role in Afghan refugees remains underexplored. This is the first study to assess attachment representations in this group using a validated narrative-based instrument.Objective: To examine attachment representations and their associations with psychological distress in a clinical sample of Afghan refugees.

pmc-12641636.title: Association Between Shift Work and Auditory–Cognitive Processing in Middle-Aged Healthcare Workers
pmc-12641636.creator: Margarida Roque, Tatiana Marques, Margarida Serrano, Alessandro Martini, Stefania Maggi
pmc-12641636.description: Background/Objectives: Shift work in healthcare professionals affects performance in high cognitive processing, especially in complex environments. However, the beneficial effects that working in complex environments may have on auditory–cognitive processing remain unknown. These professionals face increased challenges in decision-making due to factors such as noise exposure and sleep disturbances, which may lead to the development of enhanced auditory–cognitive resources.

pmc-13140554.title: From Nerves to Vessels: Unmasking Churg‐Strauss Behind Polyneuropathy
pmc-13140554.creator: Hiba Antar, Sylvana Balhas, Zeinab El Mawla
pmc-13140554.description: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA), formerly Churg‐Strauss vasculitis, is a rare systemic autoimmune disease. Neurological involvement is a significant complication. This report details a case of EGPA with severe, progressive polyneuropathy and atypical serological findings, highlighting diagnostic challenges and the importance of early intervention. A 55‐year‐old male with asthma and uncontrolled diabetes presented with progressive neuropathic pain and paraplegia.

pmc-13265613.title: When Treatment Turns to Stone: Injection‐Site Calcinosis Associated With Interferon‐β in Multiple Sclerosis: A Case Report
pmc-13265613.creator: Anna Walter, Adam Bott, Marianne Kiechle, Margret Hund‐Georgiadis
pmc-13265613.description: Injection‐site calcinosis is a rare complication of interferon‐β therapy in multiple sclerosis. We report a 52‐year‐old woman with stable bilateral gluteal calcifications after long‐term subcutaneous interferon‐β‐1b therapy. Findings were most consistent with probable dystrophic calcinosis cutis secondary to chronic repeated injection‐site trauma.

pmc-13397772.title: Integrative single-cell and bulk analyses reveal ATF4-associated immune suppression and WNT/β-catenin signaling in osteosarcoma
pmc-13397772.creator: Xiaomin Ding, Feihu Chen, Jin Zhou, Dawei Xu
pmc-13397772.description: BackgroundOsteosarcoma (OS) is highly heterogeneous and often exhibits an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, contributing to poor outcomes. The cell-type-resolved role of the ATF/CREB stress-response network, particularly ATF4, remains unclear in OS.MethodsWe integrated public OS single-cell RNA-seq and bulk transcriptome cohorts. Single-cell analyses included malignant program discovery (cNMF), regulon inference (SCENIC), and cell-cell communication (CellChat).
